evidence.source: 李學勤主編《字源》；白于藍撰「上」條
evidence.field: 上部 / 上 / 字形與用例；PDF p.14, printed p.2
evidence.text: The scanned entry identifies 上 as an indicative graph: oracle forms place a short horizontal mark above a longer line to indicate the upper position. It describes Spring-and-Autumn forms with an added vertical stroke, varied Warring States forms, and the original spatial sense contrasted with 下. I inspected the supplied scan pixels: the 上 headword, glyph sequence and labels, and the prose through the entry’s end; page 15 begins 帝, so this is not a continuation. The listed underlying glyph dictionaries were not separately consulted. No OCR error was found.
evidence.title: 字源, 李學勤主編, 天津古籍出版社 / 遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692; PDF p.14, printed p.2

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (Chinese Etymology), CUHK
evidence.field: 漢字甲骨部件分析 / 上 / 字形與用例, lines 130–135
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 上 as a short mark above a reference line and says some oracle forms place it above a curved line, later often changed to a horizontal line. It reports early oracle and bronze forms resembling 二, with a vertical stroke added in many late Spring-and-Autumn forms to distinguish 上 from 下 and 二. It reports Shang examples including 上帝 and 上甲. These are the dictionary’s analyses and reported examples, not direct inspection of the named artifacts.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫 — 漢字甲骨部件分析

evidence.source: Taiwan Ministry of Education, 異體字字典
evidence.text: The entry reports that the received Da Xu Shuowen edition gives 丄 as the head form, while the Duan commentary edition prints 二; both preserve the analysis of 上 as indicative and associate it with high/above. It also records later senses including elevated position, rank, ruler/emperor and upward movement. This documents the received lexicographic record and its glosses, not a dated semantic sequence or independent evidence for Shang-period graphic history.
evidence.title: 教育部《異體字字典》 — 上

evidence.source: 全字庫 CNS11643, Taiwan Ministry of Digital Affairs
evidence.field: 字形資訊 U+4E0A / 國語讀音
evidence.text: The official character record identifies 上 as U+4E0A and lists Mandarin readings shǎng and shàng. This supports current reading metadata, not an ancient sound relationship or graphic origin.
evidence.title: 全字庫 CNS11643 — 字形資訊 [上] U+4E0A

evidence.field: 說文解字 and 說文解字注 entries for 上
evidence.text: The page presents the received Shuowen wording ‘高也。此古文上、指事也’ and ‘篆文丄’, then gives Duan Yucai’s correction that the older form should be 𠄞 and the seal form 丄. It also summarizes differing component analyses, including positional-marker interpretations. This is a modern reference page reproducing historical lexicographic material and later commentary, not an inspected early manuscript.
evidence.title: 上 - 漢字私註

gaps: The early reference line is described as curved in the CUHK account and horizontal in 字源. Both support a positional mark above a reference line, but no primary artifact image was inspected here to adjudicate that variation.
The named oracle-bone examples reported by CUHK were not independently inspected at artifact level; treat them as the dictionary’s reports.
The supplied Unicode character-specific Unihan endpoint for U+4E0A was inaccessible. CNS11643 independently lists shǎng and shàng, but does not verify the supplied local Unihan row through Unicode.

The received Shuowen text and Duan commentary were consulted through modern online reproductions, not early manuscript witnesses. Shuowen records historical lexicographic analysis rather than proof of the Shang-period graphic history.
Sources report spatial and authority-related uses as well as upward movement, but do not establish a dated semantic sequence among them.
